bug_semantics: From Renovate 43.65.0 until 43.102.11, bazel-module and bazelisk lockfile updates (including lockFileMaintenance) ran `bazel mod deps` via exec with no allowedUnsafeExecutions gate. Bazel module extensions may execute repo/dependency code (for example ctx.execute), so a malicious MODULE.bazel dependency processed during lockfile regeneration could run attacker-controlled code in the Renovate worker. The first-party advisory GHSA-5vjq-5jmg-39xq and CVE-2026-76226 (VulnCheck CNA, state PUBLISHED) describe this as CWE-78/CWE-94 RCE; it is not withdrawn.
flaw_origin: PR #41507 first implemented bazel-module updateArtifacts by calling await exec('bazel mod deps', execOptions) with only bazelisk toolConstraints and no unsafe-exec allowlist. That production exec is the RCE sink; later PR-internal commits exported it, enabled supportsLockFileMaintenance, and moved the same call into updateBazelLockfile() in lockfile.ts. The squash landing on main is 2f71422620092e3e1e47ad9452148b93f1fcd8ca (tag 43.65.0). The patch in 4d2d86f9024e0c64dfe45a4565e23524253ba6c4 refuses the command unless allowedUnsafeExecutions includes bazelModDeps.
